title: Elementary positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions
main_claim: For every natural unit interval graph G, chi_G(X;q) is e-positive over N[q] (the Shareshian–Wachs refined Stanley–Stembridge conjecture). A terminating map theta_G: D_G^0 -> partitions gives chi_G = sum_{sigma in D_G^0} q^{ginv(sigma)} e_{theta(sigma)}. The proof has four steps: (i) a graph-alphabet quantum-torus reduction, [e_lambda]chi = v^M [X_u] m_lambda(Y); (ii) a quantum scattering diagram with initial walls D_p, with positivity of theta sections proved via a positive-reordering (COHA/PBW) theorem; (iii) the identification m_lambda(Y) = Theta_{sum lambda_i d_i} in a triangular chart graph, using repeated rotations (mutations); (iv) a packet-switch / history bijection plus Garsia–Milne-type cancellation to extract the individual witness.

issues.location: Section 3 (Theorem alg:reordering, Lemmas alg:detection, alg:coproduct, alg:pbw)
issues.description: Section 3 rebuilds, in its own terms, the integrality and positivity of quantum wall functions: the PBW structure on each slope via a separated-center filtration and a signed cocommutative bialgebra. I only skimmed it. I found no failing step: parity/unit-type matching, string commutator [D,T]=id, slope commutativity and the Hilbert-series bookkeeping all check out. But the filtration/detection arguments are dense and not independently verified. The result is consistent with known theorems (Davison–Meinhardt integrality, Davison–Mandel quantum theta positivity), so even a local flaw would likely be repairable by citation.
issues.evidence: Checked: E_{p,k} and H_{p,k} coefficient formulas; chi(e_i,e_i)=1 for E and 0 for H, matching odd->E and even->H; slope factor times commuting same-slope monomials gives the unit product; k=u(d)-2h integral. Did not verify Lemma alg:detection's divisibility argument or the multiplicativity of Delta in detail.

Computed:
- (python/sympy) e-expansions of chi_G(q) for 9 graphs with n<=5, all e-positive. In each case the sum of e-coefficients equals the D_G^0 generating function sum q^{ginv}, as Theorem 1.1 needs.
- Brute force over gap coefficients for triangular charts D=2..5: every stationary weight-one candidate (2 for D=4, 3 for D=5) pairs trivially with all its positively used gaps, so none violates Lemma tri:linear's key claim.
